title: Base change for an arbitrary morphism, against an open immersion
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ and the geometric data of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type carrying that ambient exceptional right adjoint datum, and let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to Y'$. On the ordinary derived categories of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the canonical exceptional base-change comparison
$$
\beta_f: Lg'^*Rf^\times\longrightarrow Rf'^\times Lg^*
$$
is an isomorphism. Here the adjoint for $f'$ is obtained using the base-changed compactification and the restricted FullCD bound. In particular this applies when $Y'$ is an affine open of $Y$.

Independently of the ambient datum, let $f:X\to Y$ be any separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion, and form the Cartesian square as above. For the finite coefficients of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], use the constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], interpreted by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. For every coefficient sheaf $K$ of the etale-origin class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], regarded as a complex in degree zero, and also for every bounded constructible $K$ on $Y$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical comparison
$$
Lg'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^!Lg^*K
$$
is an isomorphism. This clause uses the relative adjunction on bounded-below complexes of etale origin; it does not assert the unrestricted ambient datum. It is this bounded-class comparison that affine-chart assembly consumes.

proof.text: Read the compactification c and its FullCD bound b from D. For an open base change, extend a sheaf on the new proper source by zero. The open adjunction unit identifies its restriction with the original sheaf. Apply clause 2 of FullCD at the open base to obtain the first vanishing clause. For a further weakly-etale object V, paste its pullback square with the open square. The projection-preserving pullback isomorphism, the coefficient pullback-square isomorphism and the same open unit identify the extended sheaf with the desired sheaf. Derived open restriction and the identity pullback identify the two direct images. Applying clause 2 of FullCD at V over the original base gives its second clause, with the unchanged bound. These are openFullCDFirst, pullbackExtensionSquare, directImageIsoSource and openFullCD in Lean.

Properness and separated finite type survive base change. View the base-changed morphism over Y′, so no quasi-compactness of the open immersion is needed. Pull invertibility of the prime through stalk maps. Apply lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint to the base-changed compactification and the bound from Step 1, obtaining D′ by eliminating its Nonempty conclusion within the theorem proof.

Here is the categorical calculation inverseMateIso and mateIso. Let G adjoint U and H adjoint V have invertible units, let delta : U ; L′ -> L ; V be invertible, and suppose e : L′ ; H is isomorphic to G ; L. In the inverse mate, the only potentially noninvertible factor is the H adjunction counit at L(G(M)). The object is isomorphic via e to H(L′(M)), so that counit is invertible by Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_of_iso. All other factors are functor images of units or delta. Thus the inverse mate is invertible componentwise. With adjunctions L adjoint R and L′ adjoint R′, Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv identifies the forward mate with the conjugate of this inverse mate, hence it too is invertible. This proves invertibility of the actual specified mate; the auxiliary isomorphism e only certifies the support condition.

Apply Step 3 to the open-extension adjunctions and the exact derived pullback square. The extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism supplies e, and full faithfulness supplies invertible derived open units. This proves fixedBaseChangeIso for the specified ordinary direct-image mate. Whiskering it with the specified extension-by-zero exchange gives IsIso of sfFixedCompactSupportExchange.

Apply lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint to the identity-open compactification of the original proper part c.g, over Y, using D.fullCD. Apply the first clause of prop-exc-base-change-proper to its arbitrary open base change, obtaining invertibility of the actual proper/open support comparison. Compose its inverse with the open-composition isomorphisms for g′ followed by c.i and c′.i followed by the proper-source open projection. The compactification square identifies these composites. This constructs intrinsicSupportIso. Transport through the fixed intrinsic realization equivalences and their derived open and compact-support comparisons to obtain realizeSupportIso. Step 3 applied to the supplied transported ambient adjunctions and the inverse specified exchange of Step 4 now gives invertibility of sfAmbientExceptionalOpenComparison. Together with Steps 1 and 2 this proves the ambient assertion.

For the independent finite assertion, use the existing proved etale theorem isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_of_isOpenImmersion, recorded by lem-sf-etale-exceptional-open-base-change. The supplied compactification and its pullback provide both HasCompactification instances. Unfold sfFiniteExceptionalOpenComparison: all comparison/realization arrows are isomorphisms, and its middle arrow is the etale comparison from that theorem. Functoriality and composition preserve isomorphisms. This works on every ambient input of the displayed transported functor, hence on both requested input classes without using their witnesses or asserting an ambient pro-etale datum.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-9f7994a1e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, all 12 steps, the main-20261015 statement, proof and unit, and every cited statement. There are no new nodes and nothing under fixes/. Shape: proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; there is no cycle; every off-route statement is declared in tool_uses. The STATEMENT-DISPUTED is correct: the blueprint says the ambient datum is cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge, but that corollary explicitly does not assert it, and the blueprint's own warnings give the elliptic-curve counterexample (A=F_r). The two-clause statement is kept, so nothing is weakened. Clause 1: the datum's own compactification is used (Nagata over an arbitrary S would need qcqs). For FullCD(p'), extension by zero, lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification and the weakly-etale localization lemma correctly turn FullCD(p) clause 2 at V=Y' and at V->Y' into both clauses for p'. prop-exc-base-change-proper and cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper then apply; that the datum over S is also one over Y is implicit but elementary. Clause 2: Noetherianity makes g finite type, so Nagata applies over a qcqs Y. The C_T=D^+_et categories are closed under open restriction, extension by zero and compact support. Step 7's lower-bound argument gives real etale witnesses. I checked the mate orientations of delta_p, gamma and alpha against def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, and lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting(2),(3) with (j0!,j0'!,Rp_*,Rp'_*), (g'^*,gbar^*,g^*), sigma=tau=id gives exactly the displayed formula for beta_f. Edge cases g=id, empty Y', f proper and f open all work. Duplicate candidates thm-sf-dual-base-change and det-sf-cohsm-base-change state different things. Minor, no change needed: the report says source.document now points to main-20261015, but only proof_origin does; the master file exists. The declared tool_uses are accepted.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type carrying the ambient exceptional
right adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and let
$g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an *open immersion*. Then the
base-change comparison $Lg'^*Rf^{\times}\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*$ is an
isomorphism. In particular the base-change comparison holds for the
passage from an affine open of the base to the base, which is what an
assembly on affine charts requires. On the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the ambient datum displayed as the hypothesis
is the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so the comparison is
an isomorphism on that class without hypothesis.

proof.text:
Choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$
of [thm-nagata-compactification], with $p$ proper. By
[prop-exc-base-change-proper] the comparison holds for $p$ against
the open immersion $g$, and by
[cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper] the comparison for $f$
follows from that for $p$.
